lesson: Microcanonical, canonical and grand canonical ensembles
title: Mean energy of a two-level system
caption: For levels 0 and ε the Boltzmann factor gives ⟨E⟩ = ε/(e^{ε/k_BT} + 1). At k_BT = ε it is 0.269 ε. At low T almost every system is in the ground state (⟨E⟩ → 0); at high T the two levels become equally likely and ⟨E⟩ approaches ε/2 and no higher: a two-level system can never have more than half its excitation.
alt: Graph of mean energy over epsilon against k_B T over epsilon: it rises from 0 and levels off at 0.5; at k_B T = ε it is 0.269.
description: The horizontal axis is k_BT/ε; the vertical axis is ⟨E⟩/ε.
⟨E⟩/ε = 1/(e^{ε/k_BT} + 1): close to 0 at low temperature, with the excited state hardly populated.
At high temperature both levels are equally likely, so ⟨E⟩ → ε/2 (dashed line).
